conviction_note: Nothing company-level and unpriced was found: the negatives (JPM/DB downgrades on tracked-channel NA weakness, record Q3 gasoline prices hitting the impulse channel management blamed in July, accelerating freight/fuel inflation at peers) are public and arrived with a -9.2% 20-day slide to a 52-week low, while the skew pays for upside (-4.13) and every staple that reaffirmed into this tape (CAG, MKC, GIS) was bought; findings sum to +0.5 and the scaled number is (2*0.55-1)*4.0 = +0.4, the two agree in sign, and the dominant risk not captured by either is a cut to the FY26 EPS range below the low end, which the 'low end' July language and JPM's 'lean on Q4 productivity' note leave open.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus revenue ~$25.0bn and core EPS $2.28-2.31 (Hudson Labs preview $25,008M / $2.28, https://hudson-labs.com/research/pepsico-q3-2026-earnings-pep-revenue-and-outlook ; tradingpedia/stocktwits $24.99-25.00bn / $2.30, https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/pep-stock-gets-a-downgrade-from-jp-morgan-firm-flags-frito-lay-weakness/cZMmCWWRBgW). Sources agree within $0.03. Against Q3 2025 core EPS of ~$2.29 this is flat, consistent with the company's own July framing (FY26 core cc EPS +4-6% 'towards the low end', Q3 burdened by a higher tax rate and cost timing, ~1pt of FY EPS from tariff refunds 'likely in the quarter'; JPM on the call: '$0.07-0.09 ... implies more flattish 3Q'), https://investors.pepsico.com/docs/pepsico-5v9wci20/media/Files/investors/q2-2026-pep-transcript.pdf. FY26 guide: organic revenue +2-4%, core cc EPS +4-6%.
positioning_check: Short interest 1.90% of float, 3.2 days to cover, MarketBeat, settlement 2026-09-15 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/PEP/short-interest, via sweep row) - not crowded, no squeeze mechanism. Baseline: 25d skew -4.13 vol points (calls bid over puts, 'upside paid'), put/call OI 0.84, event-implied move 3.41% (straddle 3.51%), spot $124.17 at the 52-week low, -27.2% from the 52-week high, run-up -9.16% over 20 sessions and -2.01% over 5. RSI was 14.8 on 2026-09-29 (https://www.money365.market/news/latest/pepsico-inc-pep-downgraded-by-jpmorgan-at-52-week-low-5268dbeb). The option market leans up into a stock that has already de-rated on the NA story.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-29 JPMorgan (Teixeira) cut PEP to Neutral from Overweight, PT $138 from $170, saying tracked-channel data show North America trends 'likely continued to underperform management expectations', Frito-Lay's salty-snack recovery 'stalled' after Q1, and PEP will 'lean more heavily on productivity in Q4' to hold guidance; it cut its Q3 organic growth estimate to 2.8% from 3.2%. Deutsche Bank (Powers) cut to Hold, PT $138 from $155, the same day. Company guide is +2-4% organic for FY26.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-09): revenue and EPS beat, NA food -2%, guide only affirmed, stock -3.26% on the window (baseline) - North America volume is the line this name trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock fell ~1% premarket that day and from ~$128.5 to $124.17 since; consensus Q3 EPS estimates fell 5.2% over 90 days (tradingpedia 2026-09-24). If it were not priced the stock would not sit at a 52-week low with calls bid. What may not be fully in consensus is JPM's own 2.8% organic number, which is below the ~4.9% reported-revenue growth the $25.0bn consensus implies once FX is stripped - but that gap is FX, not a measurable miss.
findings.independence: Stocktwits writeup of the same JPM note (same document): https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/pep-stock-gets-a-downgrade-from-jp-morgan-firm-flags-frito-lay-weakness/cZMmCWWRBgW. Independently, BNP Paribas Exane cut its PT to $161 citing 'demand softness in North America' on 2026-09-23 (https://www.tradingpedia.com/2026/09/24/pepsico-holds-130-lows-ahead-of-oct-8-earnings-call/).

findings.finding: US gasoline set monthly records through Q3 2026 (August the most expensive August ever, every day above $4; September average $4.33, a record by 50 cents; $4.41 on 2026-10-01), while on 2026-07-09 management attributed the Q2 shortfall in impulse/convenience channels to gas prices and said gas 'will, at one point, come down... hopefully less of an issue second half of the year' - the relief management leaned on did not come during PEP's Q3 (ended 2026-09-05).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 was the quarter the gas/impulse-channel explanation first appeared; the stock fell -3.26% (baseline) and the July 10 note flow cut PTs (Evercore $150, UBS $159).
findings.why_not_priced: Gas prices are the most public series there is, and the stock's -9% slide since mid-September shows the NA-consumer worry is in the price; what could still be unpriced is that management's own H2 'acceleration' framing explicitly depended on gas easing, so a Q3 that misses PFNA/PBNA volume plus a softer Q4 tone would be consistent with this series. Macro-to-company transmission, not confirmed by the company or a counterparty.
findings.independence: Proxy. AAA August record: https://gasprices.aaa.com/gas-prices-remain-high-as-august-will-likely-set-new-record/ (same publisher). Management's dependence on gas: https://investors.pepsico.com/docs/pepsico-5v9wci20/media/Files/investors/q2-2026-pep-transcript.pdf (shared with the bar and the refund finding).

findings.finding: The ~1 point of FY26 EPS growth from IEEPA tariff refund claims that the CFO said would come 'likely in the quarter' (Q3) is very likely realised: CBP had distributed ~$122bn of ~$135bn of claims accepted in CAPE phases 1-2 by 2026-09-11; only finally-liquidated entries needing court orders wait for Phase III on 2026-10-06. The refund sits inside the reaffirmed guide and the flat Q3 consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior PEP print has turned on a refund; on the stage's resolved days four refund names split up or down entirely on guidance direction.
findings.source_date: 2026-09 (post 2026-09-15 CBP declaration; page cites status as of 2026-09-11)
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: the company told the market in July, management said refunds offset commodity inflation rather than raise the guide, and Q3 consensus is flat to last year as the July math implied. The only unpriced element would be a residual portion of older liquidated entries slipping into Q4 (small, and PEP's import exposure is limited), so this sits near zero.
findings.independence: Company side: Q2 2026 transcript p.8 (shared document with the bar). Refund-system side: Thompson Coburn 2026-09-17 note on Phase 3 launch, https://www.thompsoncoburn.com/insights/88-september-17-2026-cbp-confirms-launch-of-phase-3-of-ieepa-refund-process/

findings.finding: Conagra on 2026-09-30 said input inflation ran ~5% in its quarter ended 2026-08-30 and is heading to the high end of 5-6% for the year, with fuel and logistics costs having 'accelerated during the period'; WTI was $90.42 on 2026-10-01. PEP flagged 'more pressure... from a commodity standpoint' for H2 in July and said Q3 carries cost timing; JPM (2026-09-29) and TD Cowen (2026-09-23) both flagged transport/commodity costs, so the risk is to Q4 and the FY EPS range rather than to a Q3 already framed as flat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: guide affirmed with 'towards the low end' language and commodity warning, stock -3.26% (baseline). A guide trimmed below the low end has not happened in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced - sell-side named it before the print and the stock has de-rated. What is not visible in the price is whether PEP can still hold the bottom of +4-6% core cc EPS; if the market were sure it could not, consensus FY EPS would already sit below the low end, and the $2.28-2.31 Q3 bar suggests it has not fully moved there.
findings.independence: Peer proxy (Conagra) plus AAA crude reference (https://gasprices.aaa.com/national-average-dips-following-record-setting-september/, shared with the gas finding). PEP's own H2 commodity warning: Q2 2026 transcript (shared document).

findings.finding: Bloomberg reported (picked up 2026-09-24/30) that PepsiCo will raise prices low-to-mid single digits on grocery-size Doritos/Ruffles bags and some sodas by end-2026 or early 2027, still below pre-February-2026 price-cut levels - a shift from the up-to-15% affordability cuts toward recovering cost inflation.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The February 2026 price-cut/affordability plan was bought (Q4 2025 print 2026-02-03: +4.93%, baseline); the July 2026 'optimize the ROI on pricing' message did not stop a -3.26% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The plan is public; how management frames it on the call is not. Read as margin repair for FY27 it supports the multiple; JPM read it the other way, as a sign NA trends are underperforming. Two-way, so small.
findings.independence: GV Wire/Bloomberg 2026-09-24: https://gvwire.com/2026/09/24/pepsico-plans-price-hikes-on-some-chips-and-sodas-bloomberg-news-reports/ (same underlying Bloomberg report). JPM's reading of it: stocktwits URL in finding 1.

findings.finding: Staples that reported since PEP last spoke and reaffirmed guidance into this tape were bought: Conagra beat EPS $0.41 vs $0.28 and reaffirmed, +3.15% premarket (2026-09-30); McCormick beat and reaffirmed, +4.79% premarket (2026-10-01); General Mills beat $0.75 vs $0.72 and reaffirmed (2026-09-23) and rose. The bar for 'less bad and reaffirmed' in packaged food is low right now.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: PEP's own last affirm (Q2 2026) was sold -3.26%, but that came off a higher base; the Q3 2025 print, also off lows with an easy bar, rose +4.23% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: Peer reactions do not transfer mechanically; PEP slid a further ~3% after these prints, so the market has not extended the 'relief' reading to PEP. If it had, PEP would have bounced with the group instead of making new lows into the print.
findings.independence: McCormick: https://finviz.com/news/397767/mccormick-shares-rise-after-third-quarter-earnings-and-revenue-beat-estimates ; General Mills: https://finviz.com/news/394678/general-mills-q1-earnings-beat-estimates-as-revenue-reaches-44-billion . Three different companies' documents.

findings.finding: Campbell's (2026-09-03) reported Snacks net sales -6% and operating earnings -34% in its quarter, with chips retail sales -9.4% (Kettle, Cape Cod) in a 'highly competitive chips category' - consistent with PEP's claim of gaining salty-snack volume share after its price cuts, but also with a soft category; for PEP net of International (~$40bn and growing ~7%), the read is close to zero.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: PFNA volume is the line PEP traded on in Q2 2026 (-3.26%).
findings.why_not_priced: A competitor losing share in chips is consistent with Frito-Lay gaining share, which offsets the category softness; nothing here is a PEP number, so it is filed small. Conagra's snacks (flat dollars, volume -3.9%) points the same soft-category way.
findings.independence: Conagra snacks volume -3.9%: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-conagra-brands-q1-earnings-call-highlights-2026-09-30/ (shared with the cost finding). Campbell dividend/snacks context: https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/09/04/campbells-just-cut-a-dividend-it-had-not-touched-since-2001-and-the-snack-aisle-is-why/

findings.finding: PEP enters the print at its 52-week low ($124.17), -27.2% from its high, -9.16% over 20 sessions, RSI 14.8 on 2026-09-29, after three downgrades/PT cuts in a week, with the option market paying for upside (25d skew -4.13) and short interest only 1.9% of float - the expectation bar has been reset downward ahead of a quarter the company itself pre-framed as flat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: 4 of 7 prints up; median absolute move 4.51%. Prints after drawdowns (Q3 2025 +4.23%, Q4 2025 +4.93%) rose; Q2 2026, from a higher level, fell -3.26%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a statement about what is priced, not a fact the market lacks: the risk it describes is that the market has priced the NA miss and a soft Q4 tone, so a print that merely holds the guide is a relief. If positioning were neutral the skew would be near zero and the stock would not be at its low.
findings.independence: Baseline skew/run-up (sealed file); tradingpedia 2026-09-24 52-week low and estimate cuts: https://www.tradingpedia.com/2026/09/24/pepsico-holds-130-lows-ahead-of-oct-8-earnings-call/ . Shares the downgrade fact with finding 1.

outside_window.finding: Planned low-to-mid-single-digit price increases on chips and some sodas take effect end-2026/early-2027; their volume and margin effect is a FY27 story.
Supreme Court to hear Rise Brewing v. PepsiCo (Mtn Dew Rise trademark) in the October 2026 term; no decision inside the window and product already discontinued.

baseline_tension: The negatives I found agree with the -9.2% run-up and are what drove it, while the skew (-4.13, upside paid) and peer reactions point up; the evidence leans mildly with the skew, so p_up sits at 55 rather than higher because a FY EPS cut below the low end of +4-6% would override it.
lessons_applied: Rule 2 / 6 (inside guidance, one-off): tariff refund finding moved +0.2 -> +0.1, filed as one_off
Rule 5 (proxy) and 7 (sign against upside skew): gas-price finding -0.6 -> -0.4, peer cost-inflation finding -0.5 -> -0.3 and relabelled guidance
Rule 9 (segment net of rest): Campbell's chips read -0.2 -> -0.1 net of a growing ~$40bn International business
Rule 1 (reaction function): peer-relief finding +1.0 -> +0.7 because PEP's own last affirm (Q2 2026) was sold -3.26%
